entries.1ac73ed10680be24: A retail company in Hokkaido within the AEON Group, whose parent company is [[company:aeon|AEON CO.,LTD.]], that sells food, housing and leisure goods, and apparel through its stores. In addition to sales, it has operating revenue, such as real estate rental income from attracting tenants to its stores. The [[term:annual-securities-report|annual securities report]] states that the company has no consolidated subsidiaries or affiliates and is a company with a single [[term:segment|segment]] (business category) covering its retail business and its ancillary operations. Sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥380,063 million (107.4% of the prior year), and operating revenue from external customers, including operating income, was ¥404,360 million.
entries.1c87cbff7550e2a9: Home Fashion (bedding, bath and toilet goods, tableware, etc.)
entries.1fd9c8581f5d78ea: This is a category that groups six product groups: women's, apparel accessories, kids', innerwear, men's, and other clothing. Its net sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥20,065 million (98.9% of the previous year), and it is the only one of the net sales product groups that fell below the previous year. The management analysis states that the clothing division was greatly affected by a decline in spending priority and that existing stores were 96.7% of the previous year, and cites sales expansion of summer demand in late summer for clothing.
entries.259aa78c06781ef5: This is income not included in net sales, disclosed as "other revenue" in the Revenue Recognition section of the securities report, which describes it as real estate leasing income from attracting tenants to the company's stores and other facilities. In the fiscal year ended February 2026 it was ¥18,825 million (¥18,006 million in the previous year), and on the income statement it is real estate leasing income within "operating revenue." The management analysis states that the newly established Developer Division took the lead in maximizing the use of existing assets and raising the added value of facilities, by attracting tenants new to Hokkaido or new to the region and improving the environment of facilities. The rental income and expenses of rental real estate were ¥4,283 million in profit, with rental revenue recorded in operating revenue and the main rental expenses recorded in selling, general and administrative expenses.
entries.2b3345dc611356bd: According to management's analysis, sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥380,063 million (107.4% year on year), attributed to the expansion of the company's share in the Sapporo area after it took over nine stores from Seiyu Co., Ltd. on October 1, 2024, and to firm performance of its discount store format, among other factors. Sales by product group were ¥312,849 million for food (108.1% year on year), ¥46,995 million for housing and leisure (106.5%), and ¥20,065 million for apparel (98.9%). In addition, rental income from real estate was ¥18,825 million (¥18,006 million in the previous fiscal year) and other operating income was ¥5,472 million, bringing total operating income to ¥24,297 million. Rental profit on leased real estate was ¥4,283 million; rental income is recorded under operating income, and the main rental expenses are recorded under selling, general and administrative expenses.
entries.3a4be08d1fe9dede: Culture (stationery, home appliances, watches, toys, mobile phones, etc.)
entries.3a99d0d0810e6841: A category that combines 6 product groups: grocery, daily, fresh food, delica, in-store bakery and food events. Net sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥312,849 million (108.1% of the previous year), the largest among the product groups in net sales. The management analysis states that existing stores in the food division were 102.2% of the previous year, and lists as product strategies the strengthened range of pizza and handmade bread in response to demand for convenient, ready-to-eat food, the launch of specialty sections for fish and meat prepared dishes, and expanded sales of the original "Honki!" series. The securities report describes the product group system as a "classification based on internal management."

entries.42e5c48b3c81189e: It belongs to the corporate group centered on the pure holding company [[company:aeon|AEON CO.,LTD.]]. The [Status of Affiliated Companies] section of the annual securities report lists only the parent company, AEON CO.,LTD., and prints its ownership of voting rights as 67.2% (of which 1.6% is indirect). The company has no consolidated subsidiaries or affiliates and does not prepare consolidated financial statements, so the figures in the annual securities report are for the company alone. The number of employees as of February 28, 2026 was 3,095, and the annual average number of temporary employees, including expert employees and part-timers, was 10,164 (not included in the figure above). Starting with the medium-term management plan covering fiscal 2026 to fiscal 2030, it has set its purpose as “becoming the MY LIFE STORE for each and every person in the region, staying close to life in Hokkaido and building the future together with the community,” and it targets sales of ¥440,000 million or more and operating profit of ¥11,000 million or more in fiscal 2030.
entries.4735dce43c05e4d3: A category that combines 5 product groups: culture, cycle, home fashion, gardening and H&BC. Net sales for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥46,995 million (106.5% of the previous year). The management analysis states that existing stores in the home and leisure division were 101.7% of the previous year, and lists strengthened sales of one-touch mug bottles and "Home Coordy Cold," which uses a cool-to-the-touch material, in home and leisure. It also states that in winter, products using moisture-absorbing heat-generating materials and original anti-slip shoes for snowy regions were sold and performed well, but this is printed as an initiative covering clothing and home and leisure together.

entries.4b8657b929db7ff6: Gross operating profit for the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥119,423 million (105.8% year on year), the total of gross profit of ¥95,126 million and operating income of ¥24,297 million. Both sales and gross operating profit were record highs. Selling, general and administrative expenses rose to ¥111,091 million (105.8% year on year), but operating profit was ¥8,332 million (105.6%), ordinary profit was ¥8,028 million (100.1%), and net income was ¥3,732 million (103.5%), and profits increased. The increase in selling, general and administrative expenses reflected active investment in people, among other factors; management's analysis states that the increase in gross operating profit, driven by higher sales and tenant income, kept these expenses within plan. Extraordinary losses, including impairment losses, were ¥3,112 million, of which impairment losses were ¥2,794 million. The balance of interest-bearing debt, including borrowings and lease liabilities, was ¥45,130 million.

entries.b51181d2b5c2e93e: According to [Description of Business], the company operates 183 stores in Hokkaido in total: 45 general merchandise stores (GMS), 66 supermarkets (SM), 26 discount stores (DS), 45 small supermarkets and 1 bicycle specialty store. Merchandise purchases for the fiscal year ended February 2026 were ¥285,829 million. According to the related party information, the company purchased goods worth ¥28,496 million from AEON Topvalu Co., Ltd. and ¥31,082 million from AEON Merchandise Procurement Co., Ltd., both of which share the same parent company, and the annual securities report states that these purchases are made at those companies' wholesale prices, “to strengthen price negotiating power through bulk purchasing.” In product terms, it worked on launching specialty sections for prepared fish and meat dishes, strengthening its selection of pizza and handmade bread, expanding sales of the “Honki!” series (“Honki! Karaage” exceeded ¥200 million in sales in five months), and expanding sales of the price-focused TOPVALU “Best Price” line. In logistics and product manufacturing, it plans to expand its facilities, centering on AEON Ishikari Process Center, which it newly established in fiscal 2021. Capital expenditure was ¥14,789 million, used for the acquisition of a trust beneficial interest in the Sapporo Naebo store, maintenance and repairs of the former Seiyu store and existing stores, and revitalization of sales floors.

entries.e04abd64bdc40b69: The company is a single-[[term:segment|segment]] company engaged in retail and its incidental operations, and the securities report does not disclose its businesses separately. The securities report's 【Description of Business】 describes the company as belonging to the corporate group centered on the pure holding company [[company:aeon|AEON CO.,LTD.]], and says that this group's main business is retail centered on general merchandise stores (GMS). The company's main business is retailing of clothing, home and leisure goods, food and other items, and it operates a total of 183 stores in Hokkaido: GMS45 stores, 66 SM (food supermarket) stores, 26 DS (discount store) stores, 45 small supermarkets and 1 specialty bicycle store. Revenue for the fiscal year ended February 2026 was ¥380,063 million (107.4% of the previous fiscal year), and the management analysis says this was due to factors such as the expanded share in the Sapporo area after taking over 9 stores from Seiyu Co., Ltd. on October 1, 2024 and the solid performance of the discount store format. In addition to revenue, there were real estate rental income of ¥18,825 million and fee income of ¥5,472 million from attracting tenants to its stores and other sites; together with revenue of ¥380,063 million, operating revenue from external customers is ¥404,360 million. It sells mainly over the counter in stores, chiefly for cash, to general customers.
